text:
alice: quick follow-up from the authn/authz RFC — I sketched a small proposal to reconcile api key scoping + service auth for Dedicated/private customers. want feedback before I turn it into an actual rfc.

josh: sending the link?

alice: pasted below. TL;DR: single token type for human+svc keys (prefix-based), explicit scope claim, and an introspection endpoint for checking runtime constraints. migration path avoids forcing rotation for existing keys.

priya: sounds promising. can you show an example header + payload?

alice: sure. example header: `Authorization: Redwood key_rsv.eyJhbGciOiJI...` where `key_` + kind (`rsv` = reserved/legacy, `svc` = service, `usr` = user). token is JWT-ish but HMAC-signed by platform for hosted; for private deployments we support self-signed certs. payload example:```{
  "sub":"svc:billing-svc@org:acme",
  "scopes":["project:acme:write","model:embed:use"],
  "exp":1710100000,
  "iat":1710090000,
  "aud":"inference"
}```

marco: i like the prefix idea for quick ops debugging (we know tokens are svc vs user). only concern: leaking afield in logs if we show raw token. can we rely on token type instead of exposing prefix?

alice: good call. implementation note: the prefix only used in SDK headers and cli defaults; servers never persist the prefix in logs — we canonicalize to token id before any logging.

sasha: how does this interact with per-project vs per-org scoping? we've seen confusing behavior where project-scoped api keys silently fall back to org-level perms in some legacy flows.

alice: explicit rule: evaluation is DENY by default. scope evaluation order: exact project scope, org-wide scope, then wildcard. no implicit fallback to broader scope unless the token contains that broader claim. so legacy keys that relied on implicit behavior will need a migration shim.

josh: migration shim idea?

alice: two-phase migration: 1) compat layer where legacy keys get a temporary derived token with expanded scopes (logged/audited) — only for hosted accounts and flagged customers. 2) notify and then require explicit scoping; compat tokens expire after 90 days.

priya: how do we do service-to-service auth (intra-cluster) — do we require API keys or do we prefer mTLS/JWTs?

alice: we propose hybrid: internal service auth uses short-lived OIDC-like tokens minted by a local service (token broker) and validated via public key. external actors (mobile, third-party) continue to use API keys. Key lifecycle: long-lived API keys for humans/admins; short-lived certs or tokens for services. SDKs should automatically renew when possible.

marco: need to be explicit about audience and replay protection. include `jti` + nonce and require `nbf`/`exp`.

alice: agreed. include `jti` and support optional `nonce` header for sensitive operations (data deletion, model rollouts).

sasha: RBAC mapping: do we keep roles (admin/dev/viewer) or move to capability-based scopes?

alice: capability-first. RBAC roles map to a set of capabilities (scopes). We keep roles for UX (console) but enforcement at runtime is scope-based. advantage: fine-grained permissions and easier least-privilege.

josh: audits and tooling: how do SRE/CS find which keys are used by which service?

alice: we expose token-introspection + activity logs. introspect endpoint returns owner, scopes, creation_ts, last_seen_ts. plus `client_metadata` (optional) that services set on minting: `git_sha`, `k8s_pod`, `region`.

introspect-bot: NOTE: introspection API must rate-limit and require auth (service tokens with introspect scope). do not make it public.

priya: concerns about introspect returning too much data (PII). limit to non-sensitive metadata and always require caller auth and audit logging.

alice: agreed — introspect returns aggregated fields and uses truncation for identifiers unless caller has elevated audit scope.

marco: how do we handle multi-tenant Dedicated/private where customer wants their own KMS/HSM?

alice: support customer-managed signing keys for private deployments. token format remains compatible: tokens have `iss` claiming their issuer; validation checks signature against configured keyset. we also support a transparent token-translation proxy for mixed fleets.

josh: SDK impact: should clients keep sending prefix? will older SDKs break?

alice: client compatibility plan: SDKs vX will keep honoring raw token strings and auto-prefix only on `rdw auth create` flows. server-side accepts tokens with or without prefix for 6 months; logs a deprecation header to clients.

priya: What about token revocation and emergency rotation?

alice: two mechanisms: immediate server-side revocation list (for long-lived tokens) and short-lived token expiry. emergency rotation: revoke signing key and issue new tokens; platform will auto-swap and fallback-check signatures for 24 hours. must coordinate with Dedicated customers.

sasha: compliance: we need KYC/audit trails for token creation + who approved wide-scoped tokens. include `creator_id` and `approval_ticket` in metadata.

alice: yes — those are included in token metadata but not in token claims; stored in the audit backend and surfaced in introspection if caller has audit_read scope.

marco: rollout plan for enforcement changes? we need a canary + feature-flag per-account.

alice: rollout: 1) opt-in enforcement for orgs (flag), 2) opt-out compatibility layer for accounts with active legacy keys, 3) gradually flip global enforcement after telemetry shows <1% compat dependencies.

josh: any performance cost for token introspection?

alice: token validation is local (signature + claims) so cheap. introspection hits DB for last_seen/owner info; we recommend caching results in edge caches for 60s.

priya: one last thing — UI for key scoping: make it explicit in console with recommended least-privilege presets and example policies (read-only embedding key, inference-write-only).

alice: will draft mockups and attach to RFC. thanks for the feedback — if no major objections I'll open a full RFC next week. :rocket:

josh: +1

marco: looks good

priya: approve

sasha: :thumbsup:
